_meta.policy: Court, Ombudsman and election proceedings involving a lawmaker, with each event linked to its source. A charge or complaint is an allegation; a person is presumed innocent unless a court convicts. Dismissals, acquittals and the person's own response are recorded alongside charges. A case needs two independent outlets unless an official court or Ombudsman page is cited. Wording is neutral and limited to what the sources state.
_meta.scope: Criminal, administrative and election cases, and rulings on a lawmaker's public acts. Private family or business disputes are left out unless they became a public-office matter.

bong-rivera.body: Sandiganbayan (cases filed by the Office of the Ombudsman)
bong-rivera.title: Nine counts of graft (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, Sec. 3(h)) over alleged conflict of interest in flood-control projects

events.text: The Ombudsman said it had filed nine counts of graft before the Sandiganbayan against Rep. Noel Rivera over alleged conflict of interest in connection with the flood-control projects scandal. The counts were raffled to six divisions of the court. GMA reported it was still seeking his comment.
The Sandiganbayan Sixth Division denied his motions to quash two of the counts, ruling the informations valid.

The Sixth Division ordered his preventive suspension for 90 days as a member of the House of Representatives, under Sec. 13 of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (resolution dated September 29, released September 30).

jojo-ang.body: Sandiganbayan (cases filed by the Office of the Ombudsman)
jojo-ang.title: 14 counts of graft (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, Sec. 3(h)) over alleged financial interest in a construction firm

events.text: The Ombudsman filed 14 counts of graft against Rep. James Ang Dit Ang Jr., alleging that while serving in Congress he held a pecuniary interest in Allencon Development Corporation, a construction firm that won P214 million in DPWH contracts and was paid nearly P199 million.

The Sandiganbayan Sixth Division ordered his preventive suspension for 90 days from the House of Representatives and any other public office, pending resolution of the graft charges. It had earlier rejected his bid to quash the information and his request to consolidate the 14 cases, which are pending before different divisions.

albee-benitez.title: Criminal and administrative complaints over Bacolod City's purchase of land in Barangay Granada (alleged violations of RA 3019 Sec. 3(g), grave misconduct and RA 6713)

events.text: Roger Ledesma filed criminal and administrative complaints against then-Mayor Alfredo Abelardo Benitez, city councilors and other officials over the city's purchase of land in Hacienda Conchita, Barangay Granada, which the complaint alleged was overpriced.
The Ombudsman Visayas dismissed the administrative and criminal complaints for lack of sufficient evidence (reported April 27, 2026).

albee-benitez.body: Bacolod Municipal Trial Court in Cities Branch 4; Regional Trial Court Branch 44
albee-benitez.title: Petition to exclude him from the list of registered voters of Bacolod City

events.text: Judge Francisco Pando of the Bacolod MTCC Branch 4 dismissed for lack of merit the petition to exclude then-former Rep. Benitez from the list of registered voters, finding no valid ground for exclusion (decision dated October 1, 2021; reported October 4).

The Bacolod RTC Branch 44 (Judge Ana Celeste Bernad) dismissed for lack of merit the case for his exclusion from the voters list in Barangay Mandalagan, stating the Election Registration Board had correctly applied the law (decision released over the weekend before February 15, 2022).

leandro-leviste.title: Plunder and graft complaints (RA 3019 Secs. 3(e), 3(h), 3(i)) over projects under the congressional solar franchise of Solar Para sa Bayan Corp.

events.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla confirmed he signed the charge sheet to start a preliminary investigation of Sen. Loren Legarda, Rep. Leandro Leviste and former Energy Secretary Alfonso Cusi on plunder and graft complaints over projects valued at P10 billion under the company's 25-year congressional franchise.
Legarda's spokesperson, Atty. Tony La Viña, said the criminal cases against Legarda and her son Leviste have 'zero merit' and are politically motivated, aimed at silencing Leviste.

loren-legarda.title: Plunder and graft complaints (RA 3019 Secs. 3(e), 3(h), 3(i)) over projects under the congressional solar franchise of Solar Para sa Bayan Corp., owned by her son

events.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla confirmed he signed the charge sheet to start a preliminary investigation of Sen. Loren Legarda, Rep. Leandro Leviste and former Energy Secretary Alfonso Cusi on plunder and graft complaints over projects valued at P10 billion under the company's 25-year congressional franchise.
Her spokesperson, Atty. Tony La Viña, said the criminal cases against Legarda and Leviste have 'zero merit' and are politically motivated, aimed at silencing Leviste.

loren-legarda.body: Supreme Court sitting as the Presidential Electoral Tribunal (P.E.T. Case No. 003)
loren-legarda.title: Her electoral protest against Noli de Castro over the 2004 vice-presidential election

events.text: The Presidential Electoral Tribunal dismissed Loren Legarda's protest for lack of legal and factual basis, saying a pilot-tested revision of ballots or re-tabulation of canvass certificates would not affect the winning margin of protestee Noli de Castro, and citing abandonment or withdrawal by reason of her candidacy for, election to and assumption of the office of Senator. A second aspect had been dismissed on June 5, 2007, so the entire protest was deemed dismissed and terminated.

eric-yap.body: Office of the Ombudsman (preliminary investigation); Sandiganbayan Second Division
eric-yap.title: Complaints of malversation and graft over alleged involvement in flood-control projects

events.text: Criminal complaints were filed by the Department of Public Works and Highways and the Independent Commission for Infrastructure over alleged flood-control anomalies.

At the Ombudsman's request during its preliminary investigation, the Sandiganbayan Second Division issued precautionary hold departure orders against Rep. Eric Yap and his brother Edvic Yap. Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said such orders are precautionary. Philstar reported that DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon had earlier named Yap a 'person of interest' after evidence pointed to him as the beneficial owner of Silverwolves Construction Corp.

eric-yap.title: Petition to disqualify him from the 2025 Benguet race over alleged material misrepresentation on citizenship

events.text: The COMELEC Second Division dismissed the petition filed by Franklin Tino, lifted the suspension of his proclamation and directed the provincial board of canvassers to proclaim him the winner.
The COMELEC Second Division issued a certificate of finality and entry of judgment after no motion for reconsideration or Supreme Court restraining order was filed within the period.

oscar-malapitan.body: Office of the Ombudsman; Court of Appeals; Supreme Court (G.R. No. 229811)
oscar-malapitan.title: Administrative complaint over the alleged use of P8 million in PDAF for Kalookan Assistance Council Inc. (2009)

events.text: The Supreme Court denied the Ombudsman's petition and affirmed the Court of Appeals, which had set aside the Ombudsman's orders on the administrative complaint under the condonation doctrine. The Court stated it made no pronouncement on the criminal complaint against him.

oscar-malapitan.title: Graft and malversation complaints over P8 million in PDAF channeled to Kalookan Assistance Council Inc. (2007-2009)

events.text: Former Caloocan Mayor Rey Malonzo filed graft and malversation complaints at the Ombudsman against Rep. Oscar Malapitan over the alleged anomalous use of his Priority Development Assistance Fund.

edgar-erice.title: COMELEC disqualification of his 2025 candidacy, and his petition to the Supreme Court

events.text: Erice asked the Supreme Court for a temporary restraining order against his disqualification from the May 2025 elections. COMELEC Chair George Garcia said the poll body respected his opinion and had done its constitutional duty.

The Supreme Court en banc issued a temporary restraining order preventing the COMELEC from disqualifying Erice from running as representative of Caloocan's 2nd district, and directed the COMELEC to comment within 10 days. A final ruling was not found.

dean-asistio.title: Graft, malversation and falsification complaints over alleged 'ghost' or anomalous infrastructure projects in Caloocan's 3rd district (about P72.9-79.2 million)

events.text: Former Caloocan Mayor Reynaldo Malonzo filed graft, misuse of public funds and falsification complaints at the Ombudsman against Rep. Dean Asistio, a DPWH district engineer and private contracting executives over projects he said appeared to have no corresponding implementation. The two outlets give the project value as P79.2 million and P72.9 million.

arnulf-bryan-fuentebella.body: Office of the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon
arnulf-bryan-fuentebella.title: Complaint over two allegedly substandard flood-control projects in Camarines Sur's 4th district (about P84.19 million)

events.text: Romeo Penilla filed a complaint before the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon against Rep. Arnulf Bryan Fuentebella, DPWH district engineers and contractors, alleging malversation, gross neglect of duty, grave misconduct and violations of the Anti-Graft Law and the Procurement Reform Act over a collapsed river structure and a washed-out seawall.

miguel-luis-villafuerte.title: Villafuerte v. COMELEC: petition over a COMELEC ruling on Miguel Villafuerte's 2013 certificate of candidacy

events.text: The Supreme Court en banc denied the petition of Luis R. Villafuerte and affirmed the COMELEC En Banc resolution of April 1, 2013.

dale-corvera.body: Office of the Ombudsman; Sandiganbayan Third Division
dale-corvera.title: Graft and malversation charges over personal travel expenses charged to Cabadbaran funds (2011-2014)

events.text: The Ombudsman announced it had filed graft charges against former Cabadbaran Mayor Dale Corvera over P362,154.85 in personal travel expenses charged to public funds from May 2011 to June 2014. Corvera had argued the trips were for Boy Scouts of the Philippines activities; the Ombudsman said the Boy Scouts' public character did not justify charging public funds.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division acquitted Corvera of graft and malversation, saying there was no sufficient evidence that he misappropriated public funds for personal use (reported September 15, 2019).

florencio-miraflores.title: Four counts under RA 6713 over alleged non-declaration of assets in 2006-2009 statements of assets, liabilities and net worth, with his wife

events.text: The Sandiganbayan dismissed the four criminal charges against then-Aklan Gov. Florencio Miraflores and his wife Ma. Lourdes, citing the Ombudsman's inordinate delay (more than eight years) in investigating and filing, which it said deprived them of the right to speedy disposition. The resolution was voted 4-1 and lifted the hold orders. The charges had alleged non-declaration of about P6 million in bank investments and four vehicles.

florencio-miraflores.title: Administrative complaint over alleged negligence in the management of Boracay

events.text: DILG Undersecretary Epimaco Densing III filed administrative charges of grave misconduct, gross neglect of duty and conduct prejudicial to the service against Aklan Gov. Miraflores and 16 Malay officials over the management of Boracay.

Philstar reported that the charges against Miraflores and 14 other local officials were dismissed for lack of merit, while Malay Mayor Ciceron Cawaling was dismissed from service (reported May 17, 2019).

bong-acop.title: Disqualification complaint alleging vote-buying in the Antipolo 2nd District special election

events.text: A resident, through lawyer Mark Tolentino, filed a disqualification complaint at the COMELEC alleging massive vote buying by Philip 'Bong' Acop before the March 14, 2026 special election. The COMELEC said the complaint had not been resolved and that filing a complaint does not automatically mean disqualification. The outcome was not found.

salvador-pleyto.body: Office of the Ombudsman; Court of Appeals; Supreme Court (G.R. No. 169982)
salvador-pleyto.title: Administrative case over his statement of assets and liabilities (Pleyto v. PNP-CIDG)

events.text: The Office of the Ombudsman found Salvador Pleyto guilty of grave misconduct and dishonesty and ordered his dismissal from the service (decision dated June 28, 2004; reconsideration denied October 12, 2004). The Court of Appeals affirmed.

The Supreme Court reversed and set aside the dismissal and instead found him guilty of negligence in accomplishing his Statement of Assets and Liabilities for 2002, imposing forfeiture of the equivalent of six months' salary from his retirement benefits.

erwin-t-tulfo.body: Supreme Court, G.R. No. 161032 (Tulfo v. People of the Philippines and Atty. Carlos T. So)
erwin-t-tulfo.title: Four counts of libel over published articles about Atty. Carlos T. So

events.text: The Supreme Court found Erwin Tulfo and four co-accused guilty beyond reasonable doubt of four counts of libel, sentencing each to a fine of P6,000 per count with subsidiary imprisonment in case of insolvency, and ordered them to pay Atty. Carlos T. So P1,000,000 in moral damages jointly and severally. The claim for actual and exemplary damages was denied.

raffy-t-tulfo.title: Libel convictions over published articles about Atty. Carlos So (Tulfo, Macasaet and Quijano v. People)

events.text: The Supreme Court reversed and set aside the Court of Appeals' amended decision, which had affirmed the convictions of Raffy Tulfo, Allen Macasaet and Nicolas Quijano Jr. in six criminal cases, and acquitted them of the crime charged.

raffy-t-tulfo.title: Guy v. Tulfo: damages in a libel case filed by businessman Michael C. Guy over a newspaper article

events.text: The Supreme Court partially granted Michael C. Guy's petition and affirmed with modification the Court of Appeals' amended decision, ordering Raffy Tulfo, Allen Macasaet and six others to pay him jointly P500,000 in moral damages, P1,000,000 in exemplary damages and P211,200 in attorney's fees, with 6% yearly interest.

joel-villanueva.title: Administrative case over the alleged misuse of at least P10 million in PDAF (2008) as CIBAC party-list representative

events.text: The Office of the Ombudsman issued an order dismissing then-Rep. Joel Villanueva from public office over the alleged misuse of at least P10 million of his Priority Development Assistance Fund in 2008.

Then-Ombudsman Samuel Martires reversed the 2016 dismissal order on Villanueva's motion. In 2025 Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla called it a 'secret decision' and said his office was examining the records.

Villanueva called Remulla's plan to enforce the 2016 order 'harassment', said he had no pending case before the Ombudsman or the Sandiganbayan, and presented clearances from both dated September 10. Remulla then said he would not send a letter to the Senate to implement the order.

joel-villanueva.body: Department of Justice; Office of the Ombudsman (preliminary investigation)
joel-villanueva.title: Complaints over alleged ghost flood-control projects in Bulacan (malversation and related offenses)

events.text: The Department of Justice began a preliminary investigation of complaints over Bulacan 1st District flood-control projects reported as 100 percent complete but found grossly deficient or non-existent, involving Wawao Builders and Topnotch Catalyst Builders Inc. Villanueva and former Sen. Ramon Revilla Jr. are respondents in two separate cases.

In March the DOJ endorsed its findings on the malversation complaint to the Ombudsman, which Ombudsman Remulla said remains under preliminary investigation. Remulla said the DOJ's recommendation to file charges did not meet the Ombudsman's standards, and the DOJ said it would keep working with the Ombudsman on the case build-up.

camille-a-villar.title: Two counts of graft over PrimeWater's joint venture agreements with local water districts (2015-2022)

events.text: The Office of the Ombudsman said two counts of graft had been filed against Senators Mark and Camille Villar, their parents Manuel and Cynthia Villar, their brother Paolo and officials of local water districts over poor water service of the Villar-owned PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation, after about six months of investigation of its joint venture deals with water districts. Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said the Villars were the beneficial owners of PrimeWater during the period.

mark-a-villar.title: Two counts of graft over PrimeWater's joint venture agreements with local water districts (2015-2022)

events.text: The Office of the Ombudsman said two counts of graft had been filed against Senators Mark and Camille Villar, their parents Manuel and Cynthia Villar, their brother Paolo and officials of local water districts over poor water service of the Villar-owned PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation, after about six months of investigation of its joint venture deals with water districts. Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said the Villars were the beneficial owners of PrimeWater during the period.

ronald-m-dela-rosa.title: ICC arrest warrant (crimes against humanity linked to the drug war) and his petition to the Supreme Court against arrest

events.text: Reuters reported that Sen. Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity, was no longer in the Senate building where he had been under Senate protection, according to Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Gunfire had been reported at the Senate the day before.

The Supreme Court en banc, voting 9-5-1, denied his request for a temporary restraining order or status quo ante order to prevent agencies from arresting him on the basis of the ICC warrant without a Philippine judicial warrant. The Court said it decided only the interim relief and that the main issues remain.

robinhood-c-padilla.title: Obstruction of justice complaint over the May 14, 2026 exit of Sen. Ronald dela Rosa from the Senate

events.text: The civil society group Tindig Pilipinas filed an obstruction of justice complaint at the Ombudsman against Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano, Sen. Robinhood Padilla and suspended acting Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca, alleging they blocked or delayed implementation of the ICC arrest warrant and facilitated dela Rosa's exit from the Senate on May 14.

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Padilla had not submitted a counter-affidavit, and that the deadline for respondents had been extended to July 23 after Aplasca asked for more time. Padilla had not yet submitted any pleading or communicated with the Ombudsman.

alan-peter-s-cayetano.title: Obstruction of justice complaint over the May 14, 2026 exit of Sen. Ronald dela Rosa from the Senate

events.text: The civil society group Tindig Pilipinas filed an obstruction of justice complaint at the Ombudsman against Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano, Sen. Robinhood Padilla and suspended acting Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca, alleging they blocked or delayed implementation of the ICC arrest warrant and facilitated dela Rosa's exit from the Senate on May 14.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said the deadline for respondents to file counter-affidavits had been extended to July 23 after Aplasca asked for more time.

juan-miguel-f-zubiri.title: Election protest by Aquilino 'Koko' Pimentel III over the 12th Senate seat in the 2007 election

events.text: Pimentel filed an electoral protest contesting results from 2,658 precincts in 44 municipalities in seven provinces after Zubiri was proclaimed the 12th winner of the May 2007 senatorial election.
Zubiri resigned as senator, saying in a Senate speech that he did so 'without admitting any fault and with my vehement denial of the alleged electoral fraud'.

The Senate Electoral Tribunal proclaimed Pimentel the duly elected senator over Zubiri, who had resigned a week earlier, finding that Pimentel led by 258,266 votes in its revised tally. It was the first time a new official had been proclaimed as a result of the tribunal's findings.

jinggoy-ejercito-estrada.title: Plunder and bribery cases over alleged transfers of his pork barrel (PDAF) to non-government organizations of Janet Lim-Napoles

events.text: The Sandiganbayan acquitted Sen. Jinggoy Estrada of plunder for reasonable doubt, but convicted him of one count of direct bribery (8 to 9 years) and two counts of indirect bribery (2 to 3 years each), with a P3 million fine.

On reconsideration, the Sandiganbayan Special Fifth Division reversed the bribery convictions, clearing him of one count of direct bribery and two counts of indirect bribery for insufficient evidence. Estrada said he was deeply relieved and reiterated his innocence.

In a decision dated November 27, the Special Fifth Division denied the prosecutors' motion for reconsideration for lack of merit, saying it would place him in double jeopardy, so the August 22 resolution stands.

jinggoy-ejercito-estrada.title: Plunder and two graft counts over alleged kickbacks of about P573 million from flood-control projects

events.text: The Office of the Ombudsman filed one plunder count and two graft counts at the Sandiganbayan against Sen. Estrada, former DPWH Secretary Manuel Bonoan and DPWH engineers over alleged kickbacks from flood-control projects. GMA noted it was the third time plunder and related charges had been filed against him in 25 years.
The Sandiganbayan Second Division ordered his arrest on the graft charge and he posted P90,000 bail the same day.
The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division issued an arrest warrant for plunder, a non-bailable offense when evidence of guilt is strong; bail may still be sought through a hearing.

The Second Division denied his omnibus motion to dismiss the graft case, suspend proceedings and remand the information for reinvestigation, and entered a not-guilty plea for him after he refused to plead (reported June 5).
The Fifth Division denied his motion to fix bail in the plunder case as premature, saying bail for a capital offense is discretionary and that he must first file an application for bail.

Estrada filed a petition for bail before the Fifth Division, arguing the evidence of guilt is not strong and that there is no strong evidence he acquired P573.75 million in ill-gotten wealth between July 2024 and March 2025.
GMA reported that Estrada appealed the denial of his motion to fix bail, saying he is no flight risk and citing the Supreme Court's 2015 bail ruling for the late Sen. Juan Ponce Enrile.

rodante-d-marcoleta.body: Sandiganbayan Third Division (cases filed by the Office of the Ombudsman)
rodante-d-marcoleta.title: Plunder and three counts of violating PD 46 (gifts to public officials) over P75 million in campaign contributions

events.text: The Ombudsman filed plunder and three related charges at the Sandiganbayan against Sen. Rodante Marcoleta over P75 million in campaign contributions he allegedly received ahead of the 2025 senatorial elections and did not declare in his Statement of Campaign Expenditures. Former Rep. Michael Defensor and businessmen Joseph Espiritu and Aristotle Viray were also charged. Prosecutors allege he unjustly enriched himself by accepting an 'unconscionable' gift.
Marcoleta was arrested and detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
After his lawyers withdrew a motion to quash the plunder charge, Marcoleta pleaded not guilty to plunder and violating PD 46 before the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

francis-g-escudero.title: Plunder, graft and indirect bribery complaint over alleged kickbacks from flood-control projects (alleged P586 million)

events.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said his office was seriously preparing a plunder case against former Senate President Francis Escudero and former Speaker Martin Romualdez over anomalous flood-control projects, after dismissed DPWH officials tagged both as recipients of kickbacks. SunStar reported both officials vehemently denied involvement.

GMA reported, from documents in Escudero's counter-affidavit, that the Ombudsman's Field Investigation Office recommended on April 16 the filing of plunder, graft and indirect bribery charges, alleging he indirectly received kickbacks of P306 million and P280 million based on the testimony of former DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo (reported May 27).

panfilo-m-lacson.body: Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 18; Court of Appeals; Department of Justice
panfilo-m-lacson.title: Dacer-Corbito double murder case (killings of publicist Salvador Dacer and Emmanuel Corbito, 2000)

events.text: The Court of Appeals' Special Sixth Division said there was no probable cause for the Manila RTC to try Panfilo Lacson for the killings, finding the DOJ's key witness, former police officer Cezar Mancao II, not credible, and ordered the case against him dismissed.
Justice Secretary Leila de Lima said the DOJ would reinvestigate whether Lacson should be held liable instead of appealing the Court of Appeals' ruling to the Supreme Court.

VERA Files' election profile of Lacson describes him as accused of being the brains behind the killings, who fled to Hong Kong in 2010 and returned after the Court of Appeals cleared him of all charges, insisting his flight was legal and necessary to avoid harassment.

christopher-lawrence-t-go.title: Plunder and graft complaint over alleged P7 billion in infrastructure contracts awarded to firms owned by his family

events.text: Former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV filed plunder, graft and ethics complaints at the Ombudsman against Sen. Bong Go, members of his family and former President Rodrigo Duterte, alleging that firms owned by Go's father and half-brother (CLTG Builders and Alfrego Builders) were awarded nearly P7 billion in government contracts from 2016 onward. Go said the real perpetrators of anomalous projects should be held liable, pointed to the Commission on Audit as the place to check, and said he was willing to see a case filed against anyone, even family.

risa-hontiveros.body: Complaints filed by Apollo Quiboloy's camp (Pasig Regional Trial Court per Philstar)
risa-hontiveros.title: Criminal and libel complaints over statements calling Apollo Quiboloy a 'sex offender' and 'sex trafficker'

events.text: Detained pastor Apollo Quiboloy, through his lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, filed criminal and libel complaints against Sen. Risa Hontiveros, ML Rep. Leila de Lima and Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña over their statements after a US extradition request for Quiboloy. Quiboloy faces cases of qualified human trafficking and child abuse before a Pasig court. Hontiveros said she was not afraid and that the focus should stay on protecting the victims who came forward.

leila-de-lima.body: Complaints filed by Apollo Quiboloy's camp (Pasig Regional Trial Court per Philstar)
leila-de-lima.title: Criminal and libel complaints over statements calling Apollo Quiboloy a 'sex offender' and 'sex trafficker'

events.text: Detained pastor Apollo Quiboloy, through his lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, filed criminal and libel complaints against Sen. Risa Hontiveros, ML Rep. Leila de Lima and Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña over their statements after a US extradition request for Quiboloy. Quiboloy faces cases of qualified human trafficking and child abuse before a Pasig court.

leila-de-lima.title: Complaint by Manases Carpio at the Quezon City prosecutor over disclosure of financial records in House impeachment proceedings (Bank Secrecy Law, Data Privacy Act, AMLA)

events.text: Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, filed a criminal complaint at the Quezon City prosecutor's office against BSP Governor Eli Remolona, the AMLC's executive director and House justice committee members including Gerville Luistro, Leila de Lima, Percy Cendaña and Chel Diokno, alleging violations of bank secrecy and data privacy laws over the committee's disclosure of AMLC records. These are allegations.

The prosecutor's office recommended dismissal for lack of jurisdiction. Carpio's lawyer said the dismissal was without prejudice and not a ruling on the merits, and that Carpio could refile before the Ombudsman.

perci-cendana.body: Complaints filed by Apollo Quiboloy's camp (Pasig Regional Trial Court per Philstar)
perci-cendana.title: Criminal and libel complaints over statements calling Apollo Quiboloy a 'sex offender' and 'sex trafficker'

events.text: Detained pastor Apollo Quiboloy, through his lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, filed criminal and libel complaints against Sen. Risa Hontiveros, ML Rep. Leila de Lima and Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña over their statements after a US extradition request for Quiboloy. Quiboloy faces cases of qualified human trafficking and child abuse before a Pasig court.

perci-cendana.title: Complaint by Manases Carpio at the Quezon City prosecutor over disclosure of financial records in House impeachment proceedings (Bank Secrecy Law, Data Privacy Act, AMLA)

events.text: Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, filed a criminal complaint at the Quezon City prosecutor's office against BSP Governor Eli Remolona, the AMLC's executive director and House justice committee members including Gerville Luistro, Leila de Lima, Percy Cendaña and Chel Diokno, alleging violations of bank secrecy and data privacy laws over the committee's disclosure of AMLC records. These are allegations.

The prosecutor's office recommended dismissal for lack of jurisdiction. Carpio's lawyer said the dismissal was without prejudice and not a ruling on the merits, and that Carpio could refile before the Ombudsman.

joseph-bernos.title: Comelec complaint: alleged Omnibus Election Code violations (Sec. 261 pars. e, f, y), 2013 midterm polls

events.text: Dolores Mayor Robert Victor Seares Jr. filed a complaint with Comelec against Bernos and two police officers over alleged election-related acts in the May 2013 polls.
Comelec en banc recommended the filing of a case in court against Bernos and the two officers.

Comelec declared its resolution denying the respondents' motion for reconsideration final and executory. Vera Files reported that a viral document claiming he was disqualified from the 2019 race was fabricated; the disqualification petitions were still unresolved, and he was proclaimed winner on 2019-05-14. The outcome in court was not found.

rufus-rodriguez.title: PDAF (Napoles) complaints before the Ombudsman and related Supreme Court petition

events.text: The NBI filed a third batch of pork-barrel (PDAF) complaints with the Ombudsman, naming Rodriguez among nine lawmakers for alleged malversation, graft and direct bribery. Rodriguez denied dealing with Napoles, said his signatures on the documents were forged, and said he would petition the Supreme Court over due process.

The Supreme Court (G.R. No. 219781) dismissed his petition against the NBI and DOJ, finding no grave abuse of discretion because the NBI's role is investigative. The ruling concerned his petition only, not the merits of the complaint. The Ombudsman's final action was not confirmed.

paolo-duterte.title: DOJ complaint over the 2017 P6.4-billion shabu shipment (alleged violations of the Dangerous Drugs Act and Anti-Graft law)

events.text: Former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV filed a complaint at the Department of Justice naming Paolo Duterte, Manases Carpio, former Customs chief Nicanor Faeldon and others over a 2017 shabu shipment in Valenzuela. These are allegations. Duterte called the filing a welcome development that would let the accusations be addressed through proper legal channels. What the DOJ later decided was not found.

claude-bautista.title: Election protest over the 2010 Davao del Sur governor race (Bautista v. Cagas) and related Supreme Court ruling

events.text: Claude P. Bautista filed an election protest against Douglas R. Cagas over the May 2010 governor race (EPC No. 2010-42). The COMELEC First Division denied Cagas's affirmative defenses (order of 2010-08-13) and his motion for reconsideration (2010-10-07).

In Cagas v. COMELEC (G.R. No. 194139), the Supreme Court dismissed Cagas's petition, holding that interlocutory COMELEC division orders cannot be taken directly to the Court, so the protest could proceed. This ruling concerned procedure only. The final outcome of the protest was not found.

marcelino-libanan.title: Graft case (RA 3019) over a 2004 Eastern Samar fertilizer purchase (P3.25 million, Akame Marketing International)

events.text: The Eastern Samar provincial government bought 2,164 bags of fertilizer worth P3.25 million from Akame Marketing International without public bidding, according to the prosecution's allegation. Libanan was then the province's representative.

The Sandiganbayan, in resolutions of Oct. 5 and 20, 2020, denied Libanan's and former governor Clotilde Salazar's requests to file a demurrer to evidence. Libanan faced one count of violating RA 3019.

The Supreme Court granted Libanan's and his co-accused's motion to dismiss on the ground of their right to speedy disposition of cases (delay in the Ombudsman investigation), per Daily Tribune. The dismissal rested on delay, not on a ruling about the merits. The exact date and G.R. number were not found.
The Sandiganbayan quashed the same charge against co-accused Salazar and Manuel Japzon, applying the Supreme Court's ruling.

janette-garin.title: Graft and technical malversation charges before the Sandiganbayan over the 2015 Dengvaxia purchase (P3.5 billion)

events.text: The Ombudsman filed graft (RA 3019) and technical malversation charges at the Sandiganbayan against Garin, then Health Secretary, and four other former health officials. Garin said no corruption was involved.

The Sandiganbayan denied her motion to quash, in which she argued that the five-year Ombudsman investigation violated her right to speedy disposition of cases. The court found the time spent reasonable.
The Sandiganbayan Second Division allowed prosecutors to present additional documents. This is the latest ruling found; the current status may differ.

janette-garin.title: Reckless imprudence resulting in homicide cases and complaints over Dengvaxia deaths

events.text: A Quezon City court (RTC Branch 229) granted a demurrer to evidence in the first batch of eight cases, finding Garin and her co-accused not guilty. The Volunteers Against Crime and Corruption said this covered only the first eight cases and that the decision was being questioned before the Court of Appeals.

The Supreme Court court administrator directed a Quezon City family court (Branch 102) to begin pre-trial in 35 remaining cases after the first judge inhibited. Separately, Justice Secretary Remulla's resolution of the same date dismissed 98 further complaints against Garin and two co-respondents. The Public Attorney's Office filed a motion for reconsideration on January 29. No later outcome was found.

mark-cojuangco.title: Ombudsman complaint by tobacco farmers' group over 2010-2012 tobacco excise tax shares (Pangasinan 5th District)

events.text: The North and Central Luzon Tobacco Farmers Association filed a complaint at the Office of the Ombudsman against Mark Cojuangco and his wife, Rep. Kimi Cojuangco, alleging plunder, graft and ethics violations over about P569 million in tobacco excise tax shares from 2010 to 2012. These are allegations. Rep. Kimi Cojuangco called the complaint frivolous and said the funds were fully liquidated. No Ombudsman resolution was found.

imelda-dimaporo.title: Dimaporo v. COMELEC and Belmonte (G.R. No. 179285): petition over the 2007 canvass, Lanao del Norte 1st District

events.text: The COMELEC Second Division ruled against Dimaporo's side in the canvass dispute for the 2007 congressional race against Vicente Belmonte, and the COMELEC en banc later denied reconsideration.

The Supreme Court dismissed her petition for certiorari. The ruling was procedural: it held that jurisdiction had passed to the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal after Belmonte's proclamation, so her remedy was an election protest there.

esmael-mangudadatu.title: Murder complaint over the February 2010 shooting of Tamano Kamendan at a Davao City mall

events.text: Natividad Kamendan filed a murder complaint at the Davao City prosecutor's office against then Buluan Vice Mayor Esmael Mangudadatu and two police escorts over the death of her husband, Tamano Kamendan, who was shot at a mall on Feb. 11.
A DOJ joint resolution found insufficient evidence against Mangudadatu, saying the complainant had not implicated him in her initial statement.
The DOJ granted the complainant's motion to withdraw her petition for review, so the dismissal stood. GMA reported this on 2011-08-15 and dated the resolution to July 2011.

jocelyn-tulfo.title: Comelec petition to disqualify five Tulfo family candidates, including Jocelyn Tulfo, before the May 2025 elections

events.text: Lawyer Virgilio Garcia filed a petition at the Commission on Elections to disqualify five Tulfo family members, including Jocelyn Tulfo, on political-dynasty grounds. These were the petitioner's allegations.
The Comelec First Division dismissed the petition as insufficient in form because the respondents' certificates of candidacy were not attached.
Comelec denied the petitioner's motion for reconsideration for lack of procedural compliance and merit, as reported by the Philippine Star.

kenneth-gatchalian.title: Sandiganbayan cases over the Local Water Utilities Administration's 2009 purchase of Express Savings Bank (Gatchalian family named among accused)

events.text: In a resolution promulgated Nov. 17, 2017, the Sandiganbayan Special Fourth Division found no probable cause for arrest warrants against the Gatchalian family and dismissed the cases against them, including Kenneth Gatchalian. It lifted their hold departure orders. Trial continued against Rep. Prospero Pichay and a former LWUA official.
The Philippine Star, reporting on the case against Pichay, again noted that the cases against Kenneth Gatchalian and his relatives had been dismissed.

martin-romualdez.title: Plunder case at the Sandiganbayan over alleged flood-control kickbacks, with former Rep. Elizaldy Co and others

events.text: The Sandiganbayan Third Division committed Romualdez, who is accused of plunder over alleged flood-control kickbacks (reported as P7.2 to P7.4 billion), to the Quezon City Jail male dormitory as a detention prisoner and set his arraignment for Sept. 16. His camp has maintained his innocence.
Romualdez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment before the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

The court's clerk confirmed that Romualdez had not yet filed a petition for bail. Plunder is generally non-bailable, but an accused may petition if they argue the evidence of guilt is not strong. The case is pending.

gloria-macapagal-arroyo.title: Plunder case over alleged misuse of PCSO intelligence funds (G.R. No. 220598, with Benigno Aguas)

events.text: The Supreme Court en banc granted her petition for certiorari, set aside the Sandiganbayan's resolutions denying her demurrer to evidence, and dismissed the case against her for insufficiency of evidence, ordering her release from detention. Two justices dissented.

gloria-macapagal-arroyo.title: Electoral sabotage case over the 2007 Maguindanao senatorial vote (Pasay RTC Branch 112)

events.text: Judge Jesus Mupas granted her demurrer to evidence and dismissed the case, which the Commission on Elections had filed in 2011. The court said only one of 13 prosecution witnesses named her and that testimony was uncorroborated. Her P1-million bail was ordered released.

benny-abante.title: Abante v. Uy: Comelec petition over his rival's natural-born citizenship, Manila 6th District, 2025

events.text: The Comelec Second Division granted Abante's petition and voided rival Joey Uy's certificate of candidacy for material misrepresentation about being natural-born, declaring Abante the winner. Uy had led the count, 65,746 to 63,358.
Comelec issued a certificate of finality on its June 30 en banc ruling after receiving no Supreme Court restraining order. The outcome of any Supreme Court petition by Uy was not found.

ralph-tulfo.title: Comelec petition to disqualify five Tulfo family candidates, including Ralph Tulfo, before the May 2025 elections

events.text: Lawyer Virgilio Garcia filed a petition at the Commission on Elections to disqualify five Tulfo family members on political-dynasty grounds. These were the petitioner's allegations.
The Comelec First Division dismissed the petition as insufficient in form because the respondents' certificates of candidacy were not attached.
Comelec denied the petitioner's motion for reconsideration for lack of procedural compliance and merit, as reported by the Philippine Star.

arjo-atayde.title: Flood-control allegations and appearance before the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (a fact-finding body, not a court)

events.text: Contractors Curlee and Sarah Discaya named Atayde among officials they accused of pushing them into irregular biddings and seeking money for projects. Atayde categorically denied benefiting from any contractor and said he would use legal remedies against those spreading falsehoods.
Atayde appeared before the ICI and filed a counter-affidavit, saying the allegations were completely false. No Ombudsman, DOJ or court case against him was found.

chel-diokno.title: Complaint by Manases Carpio at the Quezon City prosecutor over disclosure of financial records in House impeachment proceedings (Bank Secrecy Law, Data Privacy Act, AMLA)

events.text: Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, filed a criminal complaint at the Quezon City prosecutor's office against BSP Governor Eli Remolona, the AMLC's executive director and House justice committee members including Gerville Luistro, Leila de Lima, Percy Cendaña and Chel Diokno, alleging violations of bank secrecy and data privacy laws over the committee's disclosure of AMLC records. These are allegations.

The prosecutor's office recommended dismissal for lack of jurisdiction. Carpio's lawyer said the dismissal was without prejudice and not a ruling on the merits, and that Carpio could refile before the Ombudsman.

gerville-luistro.title: Complaint by Manases Carpio at the Quezon City prosecutor over disclosure of financial records in House impeachment proceedings (Bank Secrecy Law, Data Privacy Act, AMLA)

events.text: Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, filed a criminal complaint at the Quezon City prosecutor's office against BSP Governor Eli Remolona, the AMLC's executive director and House justice committee members including Gerville Luistro, Leila de Lima, Percy Cendaña and Chel Diokno, alleging violations of bank secrecy and data privacy laws over the committee's disclosure of AMLC records. These are allegations.

The prosecutor's office recommended dismissal for lack of jurisdiction. Carpio's lawyer said the dismissal was without prejudice and not a ruling on the merits, and that Carpio could refile before the Ombudsman.

emmarie-dizon.title: Ombudsman (Visayas) complaint alleging plunder, graft and falsification over a Mandaue reclaimed property, filed against Rep. Emmarie Ouano-Dizon and her husband

events.text: Edward Ligas filed plunder, anti-graft, falsification of public documents and SALN complaints at the Office of the Ombudsman-Visayas. He alleges that the couple acquired reclaimed property belonging to Mandaue City and profited from selling it to Foton Motors for P20 million in 2012. These are allegations.
Ouano-Dizon said the couple had not done anything wrong or illegal and described buying land from a private developer as no crime. No Ombudsman resolution was found.

lolita-javier.title: Ong v. Javier (HRET Case No. 19-023): quo warranto petition over her residency, Leyte 2nd District

events.text: Former Rep. Henry Ong filed a petition for quo warranto at the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal, alleging that Javier, who won the May 2019 election, was not a resident of the district.

The tribunal granted Javier's motion to file a demurrer to evidence and dismissed the petition for lack of clear and convincing evidence, according to the tribunal's case list for 2019 to 2022. The exact date is not shown there.

ronald-singson.title: Hong Kong drug-trafficking case over cocaine found at the airport, 2010

events.text: Ronald Singson, then a sitting representative, pleaded guilty in Hong Kong's District Court to trafficking about 6.7 grams of cocaine into Hong Kong, after being caught at the airport in July 2010. He testified that he used cocaine on and off since 2004 and apologized to the court. Sentencing was pending when this was reported, and the sentence was not confirmed here.

ronald-singson.title: Baterina v. HRET, Comelec and Singson (G.R. No. 210303): challenge over his 2013 election after the Hong Kong conviction

events.text: His 2013 rival, Bertrand Baterina, asked the Supreme Court to nullify Singson's proclamation, arguing that the HRET and Comelec should have disqualified him over the Hong Kong drug-trafficking conviction. The HRET had dismissed Baterina's petition in August 2013 as filed out of time.

The Supreme Court dismissed Baterina's petition, finding no grave abuse of discretion by the Comelec and HRET and that the HRET had no jurisdiction over the late petition, according to a summary of the decision.

celso-regencia.title: Murder and frustrated murder complaints over the December 2014 ambush of then-Rep. Vicente Belmonte Jr.'s convoy

events.text: The Department of Justice found probable cause to charge Regencia, then Iligan City mayor, and others with three counts of murder and four counts of frustrated murder over the ambush. He was detained from October 2015.

The DOJ reversed its earlier resolution, finding a suspect-turned-witness's affidavits inconsistent and inadmissible, ordered the complaints dismissed and directed the withdrawal of the informations in court. The ruling was released in January 2017.

celso-regencia.title: Usurpation of official functions case at the Sandiganbayan for acting as mayor while detained in 2015

events.text: The Sandiganbayan Seventh Division found Regencia guilty of usurpation of official functions (Article 177, Revised Penal Code) for continuing to act as mayor from November 2015 while detained, and sentenced him to two months and one day up to one year and eight months in prison. The case was filed by the Ombudsman in 2017.
The Sandiganbayan was reported to have denied his motion for reconsideration and kept the conviction. Whether he appealed to the Supreme Court, and whether the conviction is final, was not found.
